items.title: Kimi Antonelli wants special photo with Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen on his wall after F1 title
items.summary: The 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix is one for the history books: Kimi Antonelli has been crowned the youngest world champion of all time, and partly because of the superlicence rules, that record will certainly not be an easy one to break.

items.title: Who slept worst last night: Frederic Vasseur
items.summary: There was at least one moment during Frederic Vasseur's post-Mexican Grand Prix media briefing when the Ferrari team principal burst into laughter. Motorsport Network journalist Ronald Vording had just asked him what felt like the umpteenth question about the evidently strained atmosphere following the first-lap clash between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

items.title: Penalty drops Oscar Piastri out of F1 Mexico GP points
items.summary: Oscar Piastri’s tough Mexico Grand Prix weekend has ended in point-less fashion, after the McLaren Formula 1 driver copped a penalty for his collision with Arvid Lindblad. Piastri’s 60-strong streak of Q3 appearances (including sprints) ended at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez as he qualified a lowly 12th, which paved the way for his troubles in the midfield.

items.title: Fred Vasseur reacts to Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc clash: “It’s a matter of respect”
items.summary: “When you are 1-2 at Turn 4, you don't imagine that you won't win the race.” This statement says a lot about Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur’s disappointment following Formula 1’s Mexico Grand Prix.

items.title: How F1 drivers reacted to Kimi Antonelli's world title: "He's made everyone else look silly"
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli's rivals have paid tribute to the Mercedes driver after he clinched the Formula 1 world championship at the Mexico City Grand Prix. The Italian finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton to secure the title with four races to spare.

items.title: Winners and losers from F1's record-breaking Mexico Grand Prix
items.summary: Superlatives are running out to describe Kimi Antonelli's unprecedented ascent to power over the 2026 season. At the Mexico Grand Prix, Formula 1's new ruler received the coronation his campaign deserved. Winner: Kimi Antonelli Antonelli's title triumph may have been a foregone conclusion at this point, but that only makes his achievement more remarkable, not less.

items.title: Toto Wolff apologises to George Russell after Mercedes "let him down" at Mexican GP
items.summary: Mercedes Formula 1 team principal Toto Wolff claimed the Brackley outfit "let down" George Russell after a deployment issue spoiled his start at the Mexican Grand Prix. Russell started from second on the grid after missing out on pole position to seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton by just 0.009 seconds, but he lost ground at the start.

items.title: Charles Leclerc responds to Lewis Hamilton's call for Ferrari talks after Mexico GP
items.summary: Charles Leclerc says Lewis Hamilton’s driving was “very much on the limit” as he defended his own move at the beginning of the Mexico City Grand Prix. Leclerc attacked polesitter Hamilton at Turn 4 on the opening lap and made it out of the scrap ahead of him. “I mean, it was definitely an opportunity.

items.title: Why Charles Leclerc didn’t yield Mexico GP lead after cutting Turn 5
items.summary: Ferrari Formula 1 driver Charles Leclerc has delved into his controversial Mexico Grand Prix drive, more specifically the way he snatched – and retained – the lead from Lewis Hamilton. Leclerc challenged his polesitting team-mate for the lead at the start, with Hamilton holding him off over the first sequence of corners.

items.title: F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali releases touching statement after Kimi Antonelli's title win
items.summary: Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali says "an entire nation will celebrate" after Kimi Antonelli became the series' youngest champion at the Mexican Grand Prix. The 20-year-old also became the first Italian world champion in 73 years, since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

items.title: Lando Norris says Kimi Antonelli should celebrate F1 title “properly” after breakthrough season
items.summary: Antonelli finished third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez to clinch the title with four races to spare, becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1's history at just 20 years and 68 days old. Norris, who won his first title with McLaren last year and finished fifth in Mexico, said after the race that he was delighted for the Italian.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton demands “serious talks” at Ferrari after Charles Leclerc clash
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton has called for “serious talks” at Ferrari following his clash with team-mate Charles Leclerc in Formula 1’s Mexico Grand Prix. Polesitter Hamilton was challenged by Leclerc from third after front-row starter George Russell lost momentum ahead of Turn 1.

items.title: Max Verstappen shares emotional message after Kimi Antonelli's historic F1 title win
items.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen says he is "very proud" of Kimi Antonelli after the 20-year-old driver became the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history at the Mexican Grand Prix.

items.title: Emotional Kimi Antonelli left "speechless" by maiden F1 world title in Mexico
items.summary: Newly-crowned Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli paid a tearful tribute to Mercedes as he became grand prix racing's youngest-ever title winner in Mexico. Antonelli took third at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez after a controlled driver to his maiden title, beating Sebastian Vettel's previous record by three years as he became the youngest driver to do so aged 20.

items.title: F1's youngest world champions
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli crossing the line in third place at the Mexico Grand Prix has resulted in the Mercedes driver becoming Formula 1’s youngest ever world champion. The Italian has achieved his childhood dream at just 20 years old, which means he takes the record from Sebastian Vettel who was still only 23 when he became world champion in 2010.

items.title: F1 Mexico GP: Kimi Antonelli clinches world title as Max Verstappen holds off Lewis Hamilton for victory
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli has written history by becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion at the Mexico Grand Prix, as Red Bull's Max Verstappen beat Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to win the race.

items.title: Five quick takeaways from historic Mexico GP
items.summary: Antonelli celebrates in style with mature podium drive What a luxury to enjoy your coronation with so little pressure. Kimi Antonelli did admit to being extra tense this weekend as his maiden world championship loomed, but all he had to do was keep it on the island to cruise to the finish line.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest world champion in F1 history
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest Formula 1 world champion after finishing third at the Mexican Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver needed to finish at least ninth in the race at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez to claim his maiden title.

items.title: Charles Leclerc's Mexico GP penalty leaves F1 fans furious for very different reasons
items.summary: Charles Leclerc’s five-second penalty at the Mexico City Grand Prix has divided Formula 1 fans. Some believe that it was far too lenient while others insist that he should not have been punished at all. The Ferrari driver went around the outside of polesitter and team-mate Lewis Hamilton at Turn 4 on the opening lap.

items.title: What does Yamaha’s shock MotoGP boycott mean for F1 in Qatar and Abu Dhabi?
items.summary: Tensions surrounding next week's Qatar Grand Prix have reached boiling point in the MotoGP paddock. There had already been unrest behind the scenes for some time, with several riders expressing their concerns, but on Sunday Yamaha became the first manufacturer to make a public statement.

items.title: Valtteri Bottas "pretty confident" of staying for F1 2027 amid Colton Herta rumours
items.summary: Valtteri Bottas is “pretty confident” of staying in Formula 1 as he batted away questions surrounding his future amid rumours of Cadillac promoting Colton Herta. The American outfit announced a contract extension for Sergio Perez but is yet to confirm Bottas for 2027, after a 2026 season in which the latter has been consistently outperformed.

items.title: Fernando Alonso 'beyond frustration' after engine issue in F1 Mexico GP qualifying
items.summary: Fernando Alonso stated that his “frustration is beyond imagination” after a power unit problem caused an early end to his qualifying for the Formula 1 Mexico Grand Prix. The Aston Martin driver took 18th with only one flying lap as his AMR26 ground to a halt through the stadium section of Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez with 11 minutes left in Q1.

items.title: F1 2026 qualifying head-to-head: Mexico GP
items.summary: After every Formula 1 qualifying session, Motorsport.com publishes each team's qualifying record in terms of team-mate battles. This record is based exclusively on qualifying results so that grid penalties don't alter the statistics. When a driver can't put in a representative lap time due to a technical issue or an incident, this will be mentioned in the table.

items.title: Red Bull drivers fear Mexico start, Max Verstappen jokes: “A Le Mans start would be just as quick”
items.summary: Although Max Verstappen said he had the pace to take pole position in Mexico City, his final run was ruined by a lock-up at Turn 13 – according to the Red Bull driver, mainly caused by Lando Norris getting slightly in his way in the final sector.

items.title: Liam Lawson disqualified from F1 qualifying in Mexico – here's why
items.summary: Liam Lawson has lost his ninth-place starting position for the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix. Racing Bulls impressed at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Saturday and managed to get both cars into Q3. The team subsequently emerged as the 'best of the rest' in eighth and ninth places, but Lawson now faces a recovery drive on Sunday.

items.title: Ferrari reveals luxury $4,300 fountain pen inspired by its bespoke supercars
items.summary: You do not need to buy a Ferrari to spend serious money on the Prancing Horse. Montblanc’s latest collaboration with Maranello has come in the shape of a fountain pen, and it costs more than some used cars. The Meisterstuck Great Masters Ferrari Tailor Made Inedita Special Edition is for sale for $4,300 in the United States.

items.title: Max Verstappen clears the air with Liam Lawson, but stays tight-lipped on Racing Bulls F1 seat
items.summary: Max Verstappen qualified fourth for the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix, but will have to drop one place on the starting grid, meaning he will start from the third row. The reason is remarkable, to say the least: contact with Liam Lawson - two drivers from the Red Bull teams during the second free practice session.

items.title: "I'll bombard myself with melatonin": Kimi Antonelli admits to driving "tense" and "tired" on cusp of F1 title
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli is hoping to overcome an off-colour Mexico City Grand Prix qualifying session with a good night's rest, but admits Formula 1 title nerves have led to him driving with unwanted tension.

items.title: George Russell identifies costly decision behind Mexican GP qualifying near-miss
items.summary: George Russell believes an extra lap of fuel cost him pole position for the Mexican Grand Prix after he missed out to his former team-mate and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton by just 0.009 seconds. The Mercedes driver will start alongside Hamilton on the front row, with Charles Leclerc in third.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: First Ferrari F1 pole “takes me back to watching Michael”
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton can finally say he has scored pole position for three different teams after a blistering lap today gave him pole for tomorrow's Mexico City Grand Prix - his first grand prix pole for Ferrari. The seven-time champion says it took him back to watching Michael Schumacher dominate with the Italian team.
